entries.072361bf62104609: In October 1991, the company acquired the Tokaido Shinkansen railway facilities. In March 1992, the following year, it began commercial operation of the Tokaido Shinkansen “Nozomi” service using 300 Series trains, and it has since introduced 700 Series trains in March 1999, N700 Series trains in July 2007, N700A in 2013 and N700S in July 2020.

entries.0a92ed93f06c79a6: It operates the Tokaido Shinkansen between Tokyo and Shin-Osaka. In the railway business results of the company (the reporting company) for the fiscal year ended March 2026, operating distance was 552.6 km; passengers carried were 183,924 thousand (commuter 13,947 thousand; non-commuter 169,977 thousand); passenger-kilometers were 60,860 million, up 10.2% year on year; and passenger transport revenue was ¥1,479,380 million (commuter ¥16,174 million; non-commuter ¥1,463,205 million), up 11.1% year on year. The seat occupancy rate was 67.9%. Non-commuter revenue accounts for nearly 99% of the total, a structure supported by business and travel demand. Considering that more than 60 years have passed since its opening, the company is advancing earthquake countermeasures covering the entire line, including derailment and deviation prevention measures, and large-scale renovation work to maintain the soundness of civil engineering structures. It began services in premium class seats (private compartment type) and is preparing to introduce semi-private compartment type seats within fiscal 2027.

In November 2016, the company applied to the Japan Railway Construction, Transport and Technology Agency for long-term borrowing using the Fiscal Investment and Loan Program to promote construction of the Chuo Shinkansen.

entries.153cfcdc997b6f0b: The head office is located at Meieki Itchome, 1-4, Nakamura-ku, Nagoya, Aichi Prefecture. It is one of the 6 passenger railway companies established in April 1987 when the Japanese National Railways Act was abolished under the 8 laws related to Japanese National Railways reform. It consists of 27 consolidated subsidiaries and 2 equity-method affiliates (39th term), and the number of consolidated employees as of March 31, 2026 is 29,569 (the annual average number of temporary employees, 7,634, is excluded). By segment, Transportation has 19,273, Other 6,691, Merchandising 2,937 and Real Estate 668, and Merchandising has the most temporary employees at 5,713. The filing company on a standalone basis has 18,518 employees (average age 37.0 years, average length of service 16.3 years, or 16.4 years when service at Japanese National Railways is included), made up of 18,402 in Transportation and 116 in Real Estate. The company has 4 labor unions: the Tokai Railway Workers' Union (18,485 members), the Japanese National Railways Workers' Union Tokai Headquarters (83 members), the JR Tokai Workers' Union (57 members) and the JR Central Labor Union (10 members). Research and development is promoted at a research facility in Komaki, Aichi Prefecture, which opened in July 2002.

entries.36be310d852e8c49: The operating length of the company's railway business is 552.6 km for the Shinkansen, 1,418.2 km for conventional lines, and 1,970.8 km in total. For the fiscal year ended March 2026, passengers carried totaled 565,579 thousand (excluding duplicate passengers between the Shinkansen and conventional lines; commuter passes 264,032 thousand, other than commuter passes 301,547 thousand), and passenger-kilometers totaled 69,724 million (Shinkansen 60,860; conventional lines 8,864). Overlapping with this are the department store and station stores at Nagoya Station, the rental of station buildings, hotels, travel and advertising, and the manufacture of railway vehicles. Capital expenditure for the fiscal year ended March 2026 totaled ¥609 billion (¥615.9 billion including amounts covered by construction cost contributions), broken down as follows: the Transportation Business, ¥571 billion at the company and ¥0.5 billion at consolidated subsidiaries; Real Estate Business, ¥20.7 billion; Distribution Business, ¥8.3 billion; and Other, ¥8.2 billion. Investment in the Transportation Business was used for ensuring safe and stable transport on the Tokaido Shinkansen and conventional lines, improving services, constructing the Chuo Shinkansen, and improving operational efficiency. Total research and development expenses included in operating expenses were ¥43 billion. The main items were running tests using the N700S confirmation test vehicle, advancing and streamlining inspection and maintenance, reducing costs for the construction, operation and maintenance of the superconducting Maglev, and refining practical technologies. For the superconducting Maglev, the company has spent a total of ¥170.6 billion from the fiscal year ended March 1991 to the fiscal year ended March 2026 as special contributions toward experimental infrastructure facilities and similar on the Yamanashi Maglev Test Line, and a total of ¥344 billion from the fiscal year ended March 2007 to the fiscal year ended March 2026 for extension to 42.8 km and equipment renewal. Separately from these, it has spent a total of ¥317 billion on the company's own superconducting Maglev technology development costs from its establishment to the fiscal year ended March 2026. In March 2026, the Superconducting Maglev Practical Technology Evaluation Committee of the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism gave an evaluation that, because comprehensive verification of the technology development issues in the basic plan has been completed, technology development under the basic plan will end.

entries.59d0cb6c44d9c93a: Operating income for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥830,167 million, an increase of ¥127.3 billion (18.1%) from the previous year. The balance of long-term debt at the end of the period was ¥4,768.4 billion, of which the balance of long-term debt excluding long-term borrowings for the construction of the Chuo Shinkansen was ¥1,768.4 billion, a decrease of ¥10.2 billion from the end of the previous period. For the construction of the Chuo Shinkansen, it took long-term borrowings using the Fiscal Investment and Loan Program in fiscal 2016 and fiscal 2017, securing the funds needed for the time being. Cash flows from operating activities were an increase of ¥748.1 billion, cash flows from investing activities a decrease of ¥621.4 billion and cash flows from financing activities a decrease of ¥150.8 billion, and cash and cash equivalents at the end of the period were ¥370.5 billion. entries.97f6d9a4f90ff266: A reportable segment that operates the railway business on the Tokaido Shinkansen and conventional lines in the Tokai region, as well as the bus business and others. The company's railway business has operating distances of 552.6km for the Shinkansen and 1,418.2km for conventional lines, a total of 1,970.8km. Sales to external customers for the fiscal year ended March 2026 were ¥1,641,663 million, accounting for 8 tenths of consolidated operating revenue, and segment profit (operating income) was ¥767,472 million, a scale that covers almost all of consolidated operating income. Segment assets were ¥10,003,296 million, the number of employees was 19,273, and capital expenditures were ¥571.0 billion for the company and ¥0.5 billion for consolidated subsidiaries. Regarding the Tokaido Shinkansen, the company explains that it completed transport for the Japan International Exposition 2025 (Osaka-Kansai Expo) and, in addition to the "Nozomi 12-train timetable", made use of a timetable that, since the March timetable revision, runs up to 13 "Nozomi" trains per hour in some time slots. It is advancing earthquake countermeasures, including the installation of derailment prevention guards along the entire line, and large-scale renovation work, and continues to introduce the N700S. On conventional lines, it completed the introduction of the 315 series commuter trains across all cars, and began one-man operation with 4-car 315 series trains equipped with a safety confirmation support device using cameras on the sides of the cars and image recognition technology. The main affiliated companies are the company and JR Tokai Bus Co., Ltd.

entries.a0fab49d9562e547: Under its management philosophy of "contributing to the development of Japan's arterial transport and social infrastructure," the company's mission is to maintain and develop as one the Tokaido Shinkansen, which carries Japan's arterial transport, and the conventional line network in the Tokai region, and also to operate "three generations of railways" by building the Chuo Shinkansen, which makes the arterial transport redundant. There are 27 consolidated subsidiaries and 2 equity-method affiliates (39th term); the reportable segments are the 3 of "Transportation," "Merchandising" and "Real Estate," along with "Other," which is not included in the reportable segments. The revenue structure is heavily concentrated in railways: in the fiscal year ended March 2026, sales to external customers of the Transportation segment were 8 tenths of consolidated operating revenue, and segment profit covered almost all of consolidated operating income. The group businesses are placed in fields where synergies with the railway business can be expected, such as JR Central Towers and JR Gate Tower at Nagoya Station, and in services that enrich the lives of customers living along the lines. The two medium- to long-term pillars are "business reform," which builds an efficient operating structure using the latest ICT technologies including AI in light of changes in lifestyles and ways of working and the decline in the working population, and "revenue expansion" through new ideas. The largest project is the Chuo Shinkansen using superconducting maglev; since the Tokaido Shinkansen has been in operation for more than 60 years since opening, the company states that it must make the arterial transport redundant at an early stage and fundamentally prepare for future aging and large-scale disasters, and that it will build the line on a self-funded basis and manage it as one with the Tokaido Shinkansen. In October 2025, the total construction cost between Shinagawa and Nagoya was expected to rise from ¥7.04 trillion to ¥11.0 trillion owing to rising prices and difficult construction work, and the company states that a trial calculation based on certain assumptions confirmed that it can secure construction funds and maintain sound management and stable dividends. At the Shizuoka section of the South Alps Tunnel, tunnel excavation has not been started; in January 2026 the company concluded with Shizuoka Prefecture, in the presence of the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism, a confirmation document on compensation and other matters in case the use of water resources in the middle and lower reaches of the Oi River is affected, and in February it concluded a natural environment conservation agreement and began preparatory work. Because sales to external customers in Japan exceed 90% of revenue, information by region is not disclosed.

entries.de1b83c36b68b50c: In December 1986, 8 laws related to the reform of Japan National Railways, including the Japan National Railways Reform Act and the Act on Passenger Railway Companies and Japan Freight Railway Company (JR Companies Act), were promulgated, and in April 1987 the Japanese National Railways Act was abolished, and 6 passenger railway companies (Hokkaido Railway Company, East Japan Railway Company, Central Japan Railway Company, West Japan Railway Company, Shikoku Railway Company and Kyushu Railway Company) and Japan Freight Railway Company were established. The company was also established at this time. In March 1988, Shin-Fuji, Kakegawa and Mikawa-Anjo stations opened on the Tokaido Shinkansen, 3 stations in total, and in the same year JR Tokai Bus Co., Ltd. was established and its automobile transport business was transferred by business transfer.

entries.f528ab433b0bb24b: The company positions the operation of high-speed railways linking the Tokyo metropolitan area, the Chukyo area and the Kinki area as its own mission. Passengers carried in the fiscal year ended March 2026 were 264,032 thousand on commuter passes and 301,547 thousand other than commuter passes, with a clear difference in character between the Shinkansen and conventional lines. Of the Shinkansen's passenger transport revenue of ¥1,479,380 million, non-commuter revenue accounted for ¥1,463,205 million, and demand is centered on business trips and travel. Conventional lines carried 395,252 thousand passengers, with passenger transport revenue of ¥106,000 million (of which commuter pass revenue was ¥32,433 million), and short-distance use for commuting and school travel is common. Some tickets are sold through other JR companies and their travel agencies, and the share of sales amounts in the company's passenger transport revenue is 15.3% for East Japan Railway Company (17.1% in the previous year) and 13.6% for West Japan Railway Company (14.5% in the previous year). For inbound foreign visitors, the company analyzed passenger trends and product usage by country and region, and expanded sales channels through cooperation with travel agencies. Because sales to external customers in Japan exceed 90% of total sales, region-specific information is not disclosed.

entries.ff9f5d952fce047c: It is the largest project currently under way. The company states that it will build the line on a self-funded basis and manage it on an integrated basis with the Tokaido Shinkansen. In October 2025, the total construction cost of the Shinagawa-Nagoya section was expected to increase from ¥7.04 trillion to ¥11.0 trillion, and long-term debt at the end of the current fiscal year was ¥4,768.4 billion, of which long-term debt excluding long-term borrowings for Chuo Shinkansen construction was ¥1,768.4 billion. The Shizuoka section of the Southern Alps Tunnel has not yet been able to start tunnel excavation work; in January 2026 the company signed a confirmation document with Shizuoka Prefecture, and in February it signed a natural environment conservation agreement and began preparatory work.
